title: The Relationship Between Vision and Hearing in Adults with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)
summary:
People perceive their environment through multiple senses at the same time. For example, information that we see and hear can be combined. Previous studies suggest that, in adults with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), this process works similarly to that of people without the disorder when sensory information is simple. However, differences may occur when sensory information becomes more complex.

The aim of this study is to determine the level of complexity at which the combined processing of visual and auditory information in adults with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) differs from that of adults without the disorder.

Participants complete a computer-based task in which different visual and auditory signals are presented either separately or together. The tasks vary in their level of complexity. We measure how quickly and accurately participants respond to the signals. In addition, participants complete several questionnaires. The entire study takes approximately two and a half hours and is completed during a single study day.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Age between 18 and 50 years
- Fluency in German
- For the ADHD group: diagnosis of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), confirmed by the treating physician and based on the national S3 guideline
- No current benzodiazepine treatment (washout period of more than three half-lives)
- No current stimulant treatment (discontinuation at least three days prior to study inclusion)
Exclusion criteria:
- For healthy control participants: current or past psychiatric disorder
- For healthy control participants: current or past substance abuse
- History of neurological disorders (e.g., seizures, stroke, multiple sclerosis, dementia, or head trauma)
- History of severe medical disorders (e.g., cancer, autoimmune diseases, chronic inflammatory diseases, or cardiovascular diseases)
- Current severe depression
- Current or lifetime psychosis
